To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

plasma 5 ‐hydroxyindole acetic acid (5 ‐HIAA), the major metabolite of serotonin in the periphery, is a good indicator of monoamine oxidase‐A (MAO‐A) activity and serotonin content in brain tissue and peripheral tissues, and this is independent of the type of MAO‐ A inhibitors used.

the plasma levels of 5‐hydroxylindoleaceticacid (5‐HAA) correlate well with the brain levels of 5HAA and 5‐Ht and with the activity of monoamine oxidase type A in the peripheral tissues of rats treated with monoamine oxidase inhibitors.
the decrease of MAO‐B activity observed in the brain after different doses of deprenyl correlated significantly (r = 0.90, p < 0.01) with the decline in the 5‐HAA content of the same brain tissue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the pharmacology of the monoamine oxidases (MAO; E.C. 1.4 3.4) and the development of a new class of MAO inhibitors.

the study of the effects of MAO inhibitors (clorgyline, tranylcyprome and deprenyl) on 5‐HT turnover and MAO activity in rat brain and peripheral tissues, and the relationship between the inhibition of MAOs and the decrease of 5‐HT and 5‐HAA levels in the brain and plasma, respectively.

the study of the effects of MAO inhibition in the rat by the nonspecific MAO‐A and ‐B inhibitors tranylcyclopromine and clorgyline and by the selective MAO‐B inhibitor deprenyl on the activity of MAO‐B in the rat brain and liver and the activity of MA‐A in the brain and liver and in the plasma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
plasma 5 HIAA is an indicator of MAO‐ A inhibition in the brain, and this may be of use in the clinical evaluation of MAO‐inhibitors.
the plasma 5‐Hydroyindoleacetic (5‐Hiaa) is a reliable and convenient peripheral indicator of MAO‐a inhibition in rat brain and tissues.
plasma 5HIAA can serve as a peripheral index of brain MAO‐A inhibition in rats, but not in humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
5‐HAA in plasma can be used as an index of brain MAO‐A inhibition.
5‐HAA in plasma is an indicator of MAO‐B activity in the brain, and 5‐HAI is an indicator of the MAO‐A inhibition in the brain.
the inhibition of brain MAO‐A by tranylcyprome and clorgyline is paralleled by the inhibition of peripheral MAO‐A, and this is reflected by a decrease in plasma 5‐hydroxindoleacetic (5‐HAA).
The main takeaway from our work is that
plasma 5HIAA can serve as a peripheral marker for MAO-A inhibition in the brain.
plasma 5-HIAA can be a reliable indicator of brain 5‐HT levels and of MAO‐activity inhibition.

the plasma levels of 5‐hydroxylindoleacetic (5‐HIAL) acid, the main metabolite of serotonin, can be used confidently in the clinical setting as a peripheral indicator for the inhibition of monoamine oxidase‐A (MAO‐A) in brain.
